newsitem.title: USA: Nuveen's Spalding says deal structure key in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Nuveen's Spalding says deal structure key in 1997.

text.p: Deal structure will be a key issue in selecting municipal bond investments in 1997, Tom Spalding, John Nuveen & Co's head portfolio manager, told a group of reporters Wednesday.
Spalding said in particular he will be looking for good call protection, strong indentures, well-defined sinking funds, and bond insurance -- provided he does not have to sacrifice too much yield.
Spalding said he sees no particular geographic sectors to watch, unlike in 1995 when California offered opportunity, and in 1996, when the Mid-West showed promise.
The fund manager also said he sees a flatter yield curve ahead, which will enable him to move in from the 20- to 25-year area, to the 15- to 20-year area with very little sacrifice in yield.

Looking back at 1996, Spalding said the Mid-West outperformed, with upgrades in Ohio and Michigan. California continued to do well in the aftermath of Orange County, and as real estate values improved.

Airports performed well, led by Denver International Airport, and tollways like Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor and the San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor. also were strong performers, Spalding said.
He said the health care sector also was profitable, especially single-A stand-alone hospitals that were taken over by hospital conglomerates rated AA to AAA.

Public power companies were underperformers because of deregulation. Spalding cited North Carolina Eastern Municipal Power Agency and Catawba electric bonds. Solid waste issues have also underperformed because flow control issues remain unresolved, Spalding said.
